title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous one. There, X̄ is the Artin–Verdier compactification of Spec ℤ, with the real place included. The étale cohomology of G_m on it was recorded as H^0 = {±1}, H^1 = 0, H^2 = 0, H^3 = ℚ/ℤ. Ū = X̄ − S, where S is a set of s finite primes. The previous page set up the localization sequence with H^i_S(X̄,G_m) = H^{i-1}(S,ℤ). This page reads off the results.

(1) Units: H^0(Ū,G_m) = ℤ_S^* = ℤ/2 ⊕ ℤ^s.
(2) Picard group: H^1(Ū,G_m) = Pic(ℤ_S) = 0.
(3) Brauer group in the Artin–Verdier sense: H^2(Ū,G_m) = Ker((ℚ/ℤ)^s →Σ ℚ/ℤ).
(4) H^3(Ū,G_m) = 0, because the sum map is surjective when s ≥ 1. H^i = 0 for i ≥ 3.

Next he uses the Kummer sequence 0→μ_{ℓ^n}→G_m→G_m→0, implicitly with ℓ ∈ S so that it is exact on Ū.
- H^1(Ū,μ_{ℓ^n}) = units/ℓ^n ⊕ Pic[ℓ^n] = (ℤ/ℓ^n)^s, ignoring the sign contribution when ℓ = 2.
- H^2(Ū,μ_{ℓ^n}) = Pic/ℓ^n ⊕ Br[ℓ^n] = Ker((ℤ/ℓ^n)^s → ℤ/ℓ^n).
- H^3 = Br/ℓ^n ⊕ H^3[ℓ^n] = 0, because the kernel group in (3) is divisible.

Passing to the limit gives ℓ-adic cohomology:
- H^0(Ū,ℤ_ℓ) = ℤ_ℓ;
- H^1(Ū,ℤ_ℓ(1)) = ℤ_S^* ⊗ ℤ_ℓ = ℤ_ℓ^s;
- H^2(Ū,ℤ_ℓ(1)) = T_ℓ Br = Ker(ℤ_ℓ^s → ℤ_ℓ).
The margin says 'petite modification pour ℓ=2 en dim 0': the unit −1 contributes μ_2 in H^0 (and in H^1 of μ_{2^n}).

Finally he gives a rational ('motivic' or rationalized ℓ-adic) table for the compactified X = Spec ℤ: H^0 = ℚ (possibly corrected; see below), H^1 = 0, H^2 = 0, H^3 = ℚ. The degree-3 class comes from H^3(X̄,G_m) = ℚ/ℤ via its Tate module. So X̄ = Spec ℤ looks cohomologically like a rational homology 3-sphere, with a degree-3 trace. Removing s primes kills H^3 and creates H^1 of rank s and H^2 of rank s−1. This is the 'knot complement' behaviour.

The page is a worked example inside a section (next page, §5) on finiteness mod torsion of H^i(X,G_m) via the divisor sequence 0→G_m→R^*→Div→0. Its purpose is to calibrate expected ranks of H^i(X, ℚ(1)) for arithmetic schemes, in the context of 'Galois theory of motives'.
errors: H^0(X, ℚ(1)) = ℚ is inconsistent with ℚ(1) coefficients: rationalized ℓ-adic H^0(X,ℚ_ℓ(1)) = 0 because μ_{ℓ^∞}(ℚ) is finite. ℚ is right for H^0(X,ℚ(0)), the dual partner of H^3(X,ℚ(1)) = ℚ. The bold overwritten symbols on the image suggest Grothendieck was correcting these entries.
The Kummer computations implicitly require ℓ ∈ S, i.e. ℓ invertible on Ū; this is not stated.
For ℓ = 2 the unit −1 adds a ℤ/2 to H^0(μ_{2^n}) and to H^1(μ_{2^n}). Real-place subtleties in the Artin–Verdier modified cohomology also enter. This is only flagged by the marginal note.
H^0(Ū, ℤ_ℓ) is given untwisted while the other ℓ-adic lines are ℤ_ℓ(1); this is a harmless mixing of twists.

ideas.what: Étale cohomology of G_m on compactified Spec ℤ and on Spec ℤ_S: units, Pic, Brauer group as Ker of the sum of local invariants, vanishing of H^3 on the open part.
ideas.modern_name: Artin–Verdier duality / class field theory computation of H^*(Spec O_S, G_m)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Verdier (1964); Tate; Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's Brauer III (Dix exposés) treats Brauer groups of schemes; the explicit Spec ℤ computation is Artin–Verdier's

ideas.what: Kummer-sequence passage to μ_{ℓ^n} and ℤ_ℓ(1) cohomology of Spec ℤ[1/S]: H^1 = units ⊗ ℤ_ℓ, H^2 = T_ℓ Br.
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic Galois cohomology of G_{ℚ,S} with Tate twists (Poitou–Tate)

ideas.what: Rational table H^*(Spec ℤ̄, ℚ(1)) concentrated in degrees 0 and 3: compactified Spec ℤ as a rational homology 3-sphere, with removed primes behaving like knots.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic topology (primes as knots, Spec ℤ as 3-manifold); motivic/Weil-étale duality in dimension 3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur (1963–64 notes, 1973), later Manin, Kapranov, Reznikov, Morishita; Lichtenbaum and Deninger for Weil-étale/dynamical versions

missed.claim: Inside notes on a 'Galois theory of motives', Grothendieck tabulates ℚ(1)-cohomology of compactified Spec ℤ as ℚ in degrees 0 and 3. This implicitly treats Spec ℤ as having 3-dimensional Poincaré duality for motivic coefficients, i.e. Ext's between ℚ(0) and ℚ(1) over Spec ℤ. It is an early, independent instance of the 'Spec ℤ is a 3-manifold' heuristic placed in a motivic setting. The idea itself is standard (Mazur, Artin–Verdier); only its appearance in Grothendieck's motive notes is undocumented.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents Grothendieck using Artin–Verdier duality as a test case for motivic cohomology over Spec ℤ, which bears on the prehistory of Lichtenbaum's Weil-étale programme and of arithmetic topology. Mathematically it is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are standard Artin–Verdier/Kummer bookkeeping for Spec ℤ_S, already known by 1964. The only mildly interesting feature is the rational 'homology 3-sphere' table inside the motive notes, but Mazur and Artin–Verdier had this picture at the same time.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Z_{??}' is ℤ/2 (written ℤ_{/2}), so H^0(Ū,G_m) = ℤ/2 + ℤ^s.
The '[-donc-]' before H^1(Ū,μ_{ℓ^n}) is a crossed-out 'alors' or 'donc'.
Margin reads 'petite modification [-pour-] ℓ=2 en dim 0'.
The values of H^0(X,ℚ(1)) and H^1(X,ℚ(1)) are overwritten in bold ink (filled circle, circled 0). H^0 may have been corrected between ℚ and 0, and H^1 reads 0. H^3 is a bold ℚ.
